Subject: Re: Follow-up: DPA clarifications and data handling (PII, retention, breach notice)

Hi Samir / Olivia,

Thanks again for taking time today — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps so we're aligned: 

- Scope from the call: Pioneer Health will use Redwood for inference (text generation + embeddings) on patient-identifier-free summaries, but a subset of metadata will be PII-adjacent (hashed IDs, timestamps). You flagged three items for the DPA: controller/processor roles, subprocessors list, and breach-notice SLAs.

- Our answers (short):

• Controller/Processor: Pioneer Health will be Controller; Redwood will act as Processor for customer-provided data processed on your behalf.
• Subprocessors: we use a small set (cloud infra, monitoring, logging). I attached our standard DPA and included a link to the live subprocessor list.
• Breach notice: Redwood provides incident notification and an initial acknowledgement within our stated SLA; I've outlined typical timelines below and can commit to a phrasing for the DPA redline.

Attachment: redwood-dpa.pdf (standard DPA)

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll loop in legal (cc: Rachel) to review the three items and provide a redline today/tomorrow.
2) If that looks good, we can do a 30-min follow-up with your legal counsel to close the DPA.
3) DocuSign link for execution after agreement.

Can you confirm: are you requiring EU-only residency for the dataset in scope, or is US-hosting acceptable for this initial pilot? That will affect the specific residency clause in the DPA.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa — a couple follow-ups while we wait for legal: 

- Breach notice: 72 hours is our starting requirement. If Redwood can commit to initial notification within 48–72 hours and provide regular updates, that will work.
- Data residency: for the pilot, we prefer US-only hosting, but eventual production may need EU residency as well. Can Redwood support EU region hosting and will that be a contract choice?
- Subprocessors: please confirm whether your subprocessor list includes (1) cloud infra provider, (2) managed monitoring (logs), and (3) analytics partners — and whether any of those process customer IDs.

Also, happy to review the redline once you share. Procurement timeline: pilot contract signed by end of month if DPA is acceptable.

Samir

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@pioneerhealth.com>, Olivia Park <olivia.park@pioneerhealth.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: DPA clarifications and data handling (PII, retention, breach notice)

Hi Samir / Olivia — quick answers and attached redline for your legal team.

1) Controller/Processor: Confirmed — Pioneer Health remains Controller; Redwood is Processor. We'll include explicit language in the DPA redline (see section 1.1 in the attached).

2) Subprocessors: Our current, publicly maintained list is here: https://app.redwood.ai/legal/subprocessors.pdf. To confirm the specific items you called out: 
   - Cloud infra: AWS (us-east-1) — we do not use any shared-model serving infra that would access customer data outside of the isolated tenant environment.
   - Monitoring/logging: Datadog for metrics and structured logs (PII is redacted before log ingestion by default).
   - Analytics: internal product analytics (aggregated); no customer identifiers stored in analytics exports.

We will provide 30-days advance notice for any new subprocessors; critical security-related subprocessors will be notified earlier.

3) Breach notice: Redwood’s standard practice is to provide an initial acknowledgement within 48 hours of confirmed incident discovery and follow-up updates until remediation. The redline includes a 48-hour initial notification commitment and weekly updates until resolved. If your counsel prefers 72 hours, we can accept that as well; 48 gives you earlier visibility.

4) Data residency: We support per-customer region pinning. For the pilot we can provision US-only hosting (us-west / us-east). EU residency (eu-west-1) is supported for production; that requires a region addendum in the DPA which I included in the redline.

Attachment: PioneerHealth_DPA_Redline.pdf (redline of standard DPA with the sections above highlighted)

Next steps:
- Olivia: if you can confirm the breach-notice window you prefer (48 vs 72) and any required subprocessors restrictions, we'll incorporate final language and push to DocuSign. Link to proposed signature packet: https://app.redwood.ai/docusign/RDW-2026-3571
- If helpful, we can set a 30-min call with our privacy lead to walk the redline (available today 4–5pm PT).

Thanks — Marissa

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: DPA clarifications and data handling (PII, retention, breach notice)

Hi Samir / Olivia — Rachel here (legal ops). Thanks for the notes. I reviewed Marissa's redline and can confirm the following operational commitments we can sign to for the pilot:

- Incident notification: Redwood will provide initial acknowledged notice within 48 hours of confirmed discovery and weekly status updates. We will include escalation contacts for both security and legal.
- Subprocessor notice: Redwood publishes an up-to-date list and will provide 30 days' notice for additions; for critical infra changes we will notify earlier.
- Data residency: we will pin the pilot to US-only infrastructure as requested; EU-hosting is available and we'll add the region addendum for production.

If that aligns with Pioneer Health risk appetite, I can incorporate any language edits Olivia requests and circulate a final DPA to sign. Please let us know whether you want the 48-hour or 72-hour initial notification window included and whether there are any subprocessors you need excluded.

Best regards,
Rachel Kim
